NUMBER: cinematic typography (monument: ghosted 520 px numeral + amber QUADRILLION; three states — arrival, receded header, return). DEFINITION: 2D flat cut ('unhappiness' tile cut into un / happi / ness). Palette and serif face follow the lane's adopted Variant B family.
records.alternatives: Whiteboard (this piece's own exp-02 specimen style) — NOT chosen: the specimen is still under the owner's judgment (Action #79); building in it would pre-judge his verdict, and the spine already carries the lane. Pure kinetic typography throughout — rejected: the number must be the only monument. Live action/stock — off-lane. Single-style purity — rejected: the piece has three distinct jobs (scale, system, demonstration); the menu exists to be composed.
records.context: Owner's style law (2026-10-26 ~11:44 ET): every video starts with a base context layer where a style decision is already made — one of the 14 categorized styles or a deliberate mix, with discussion, reasoning, and context recorded. Lane adoption #78: Variant B (the A59 grammar) is the Word Definitions direction. Reference for the number treatment: soa-01's exp-02 cinematic-typography specimen.
records.why: Each pick has a named job: the A59 spine gives the piece a persistent OBJECT the viewer learns (the token piece) and keeps lane consistency; cinematic typography gives the owner's hook/bookend number the scale his structure demands; the 2D cut makes the one teaching idea visible instead of merely said.

records.choice: The hook is the sourced fact, in its sourced form: 'More than three point two quadrillion' tokens processed by Google's machines every month — Sundar Pichai, Google I/O 2026 keynote (May 2026), across all Google AI surfaces. Trajectory (9.7T/mo 2024 → 480T/mo 2025 → 3.2 quadrillion/mo 2026, ≈330× in two years) is sourcing context, NOT narration. Scope note carried: processed ≠ unique generated text. On-screen source line: 'Source: Google I/O 2026 · tokens processed across Google's AI surfaces'.
records.alternatives: Rounding to 'quadrillions of tokens' without the figure — rejected: the owner's excitement IS the figure's scale; a vague plural spends it. Putting the 330× trajectory in narration — rejected: a second number competes with the hook's.
records.context: Fact verified and supplied with the job brief, with its scope note from the Workshop Opening's sourcing.
records.why: A fact at full scale is the strongest honest hook the owner's structure allows; carrying it in sourced form keeps the piece's claim exactly as strong as its evidence.
records.change: Replaces the delivered build's hook (cold definition question) for the redeveloped build.

records.choice: Bookend: hook number (L1) → entry question (L2) → definition (L3) → machine's-eye + rule (L4) → performed count (L5) → stakes (L6) → turn: machines think in tokens (L7) → the number returns (L8): 'More than three point two quadrillion of those — every month. Now you know what one is.' The monument object performs the same arc visually (full scale → receded → full scale + digit expansion + the single token tile).
records.alternatives: The lane's definition-by-correction arc (delivered build) — superseded for this piece by the owner's explicit structure. A fresh closing fact instead of the return — rejected: the owner directed the COME-BACK; recognition is the payoff.
records.context: Owner's direction (2026-10-26): 'use that number to tell the story of what the token is AND come back to it at the end'.
records.why: The return converts the hook from a claim into a measurement the viewer can now read: at L8 they know what ONE of the 3.2 quadrillion is.
records.change: Story structure of record for the redeveloped build (metadata.json story_structure).

records.choice: Script i3 (transcript/source-script.md): 8 lines, 132 spoken words. Stage-1 decisions: the settled definition essence carries verbatim ('a chunk of text…'); the stakes survive compressed (all four — reads/writes/pay/hold — because they are what make the bookend's number matter); the 'three-quarters of a word' gloss is DROPPED (two numeric glosses on one rule is one too many; the performed count teaches size); the cold question becomes L2 (earned by the hook); i2's restatement close is absorbed by the bookend (never close twice); navigation 0 words.
records.alternatives: Keeping the gloss — rejected (see choice). Dropping a stake — rejected: each stake is a different reason the unit matters, and L6's list is the turn's fuel.
records.context: Two-stage model: content settles first, delivery as a separate pass. Editor pass run on the draft — PASS, six findings dispositioned in the script doc (incl. two deliberate keeps: the owner's own phrasings).
records.why: Content discipline is what makes the clone read with intonation (owner's standing fix direction: better-developed transcripts generate better audio).
records.change: i3 is the redeveloped build's script of record; i2/delivered-6 preserved at transcript/superseded/.

records.choice: Pause map with researched sizes (files/pause-transition-doctrine.md): F1 500 ms standard joints; ONE F3 viewer-think beat 1,300 ms after the entry question (the piece's single think beat — the hook has already done the exciting; the question is where the viewer must think); F4 900 ms suspense before the count and before the bookend; F2 1,000 ms at the turn. Realized gaps = the decided classes BY CONSTRUCTION (starts re-locked to measured fitted takes). Narration starts at the container's 2.00 s; pauses are narration-only, the bed never gates.
records.alternatives: Locking starts from wps estimates and letting realized gaps float — rejected: an unmeasured gap is an unchosen pause (the exact randomness the doctrine names). More think beats — rejected: one question, one beat; suspense beats (F4) carry the other two joints.
records.context: Doctrine classes F1–F7 with researched ranges; fit standard (fit-proof-2) for the take measurements the re-lock consumed.
records.why: Delivery is decided, measured, and reproducible — not inherited from wherever the TTS happened to breathe.
records.change: Delivery structure of record (metadata.json delivery_structure; script i3 §3).

records.choice: The performed count counts FIVE tokens in 'The machine reads tokens.': The / machine / reads / tokens / the full stop. The scene performs exactly five landings (four word tiles + the full-stop tile) and the counter locks on 5 as 'Five tokens.' is spoken.
records.alternatives: Counting four (words only) — factually wrong for tokenization and would teach the wrong lesson. Splitting a word (e.g. 'tok-ens') — a different tokenizer's choice; the full-stop fifth is the canonical, checkable demonstration (the standard GPT-family tokenization of this sentence) and the more delightful beat (punctuation counts too).
records.context: The piece's settled teaching: a token is a chunk of text the machine counts — punctuation is text the machine counts.
records.why: The count must be TRUE, or the piece teaches a falsehood at its most memorable moment.
records.change: Settles the count for the redeveloped build; the scene's tile choreography and word-decision records 70–75 carry it.
